name: sugarcane
sowing_season: Spring: February–March (North India) | Suru: January–February | Adsali: July–August (Maharashtra, 15–18 months) | Autumn: October
harvest_season: 10–12 months after planting (adsali 15–18 months), mostly November–April
soil: Deep, well-drained loam to clay loam, pH 6.5–7.5; avoid waterlogged and saline fields

stages.name: Germination
stages.description: Buds on the planted setts sprout and the first shoots come up.
stages.irrigation: Irrigate right after planting, then lightly every 7–10 days. Keep the soil moist, not flooded.
stages.fertilizer: Basal at planting: 8–10 tonnes FYM or compost + 50 kg DAP + 40 kg MOP per acre in the furrows.
watch_for: Early shoot borer — the central shoot dries (dead heart)
Gaps where setts did not sprout
tips: Use 2–3 bud setts from a healthy 8–10 month old crop
Dip setts in Carbendazim 1 g/litre for 10 minutes before planting
Fill gaps with pre-sprouted setts within 30 days

stages.name: Tillering
stages.description: Each sprouted bud sends out side shoots (tillers). The number of canes is decided now.
stages.irrigation: Every 7–10 days in summer — this is the most water-sensitive stage. Drip saves 40–50% water.
stages.fertilizer: Urea in two splits: 50 kg per acre at 45 days and 50 kg per acre at 90 days, each with light earthing up.
tips: Keep the field weed-free till 120 days
Spread dry trash between rows as mulch to save water and check weeds
Pull out and destroy dead hearts with the larva inside

stages.name: Grand Growth
stages.description: Fastest growth: canes lengthen and add weight, mostly in the monsoon.
stages.irrigation: Every 10–15 days when there is no rain. Drain standing rain water quickly.
stages.fertilizer: Last urea dose of 35 kg per acre by 120–150 days, with full earthing up. No nitrogen after that.
watch_for: Woolly aphid — white woolly coating under leaves
Red rot — top leaves dry, the split cane is red with white patches and smells sour
tips: Do full earthing up before the monsoon
Tie the canes of two rows together (propping) to stop lodging
Remove dry lower leaves (detrashing) at 5 and 7 months

stages.name: Maturity / Ripening
stages.description: Growth slows and sugar builds up in the canes.
stages.irrigation: Reduce irrigation; stop 15–20 days before harvest.
tips: Check ripeness with a hand refractometer — harvest when the Brix reading is 18 or more
Cut canes close to the ground and send them to the mill within 24 hours
For a good ratoon crop, shave the stubbles and apply fertilizer soon after harvest

common_pests.name: Early shoot borer
common_pests.symptoms: Central shoot of young plants dries and pulls out easily (dead heart) with a bad smell
common_pests.control: Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR 7.5 kg per acre in the soil near the plants, then a light irrigation

common_pests.name: Termites
common_pests.symptoms: Setts and young plants eaten from inside, shoots dry up
common_pests.control: Chlorpyriphos 20 EC 1–2 litres per acre sprayed on the setts in the furrows at planting

common_pests.name: Woolly aphid
common_pests.symptoms: White woolly insects under leaves, black sooty mould
common_pests.control: Release the predators Dipha aphidivora or Micromus (ask your sugar factory or KVK); avoid broad sprays that kill them

common_diseases.name: Red rot
common_diseases.symptoms: Top leaves dry; the split cane is red with white cross-bands and smells of alcohol
common_diseases.control: No cure in the field — uproot and burn affected clumps, plant resistant varieties and healthy setts, and do not keep a ratoon of an affected field

common_diseases.name: Smut
common_diseases.symptoms: A long black whip comes out from the top of the cane
common_diseases.control: Cover the whip with a bag, pull out the clump and burn it; use healthy setts

common_diseases.name: Wilt
common_diseases.symptoms: Leaves yellow and dry, canes become hollow and light
common_diseases.control: Use healthy setts dipped in Carbendazim 1 g/litre, avoid water stress, rotate crops
